chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Mahboub, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Every slave who is tortured with, so he is free.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a slave's freedom if their master tortures them?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'tadil' (compensation through emancipation), where specific physical impairments or tortures inflicted by a master automatically grant the slave freedom. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the master's liability for the slave's well-being, treating the injury as a debt paid by releasing the slave from bondage.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Ja’far Bin Mahboub, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Every slave who is tortured with, so he is free’.
